summary: One plugin for a mixture of experts larger than the device: it decides where the routed experts live (device, host memory, a file), keeps those routed last in a device cache that takes every byte the device has free while the engine serves, computes misses on the CPU while the link copies them in beside the round, and runs a routed layer in one call
implementation_scope: ExpertOffload (code/offload.py): the decision tree (choose_tier, cache_slots, choose_misses), FileStore for the disk tier, the one-call forward over device-expert-cache's ExpertCache under recent residency, expert-tensors' BundleStore, host-expert-tier's CpuTier behind heterogeneous-expert-dispatch's DeviceDispatch and grouped-experts' kernel (KernelRoutes); the cache's memory through the device's memory (crit_plugins.memory: the cache is an elastic range and a giver, filled once Core says the load is over) and the device's step frames (Core's: the device keeps the run's headroom and gives a prompt step the room its chunk was measured to take, the cache giving and growing back) or a KV pool's spare bytes and idle pages; route recording, routing profiles and a one-line diagnosis. code/bench.py runs the plugin alone on a store file and a recorded trace. No arithmetic of its own: every row is grouped-experts' kernel or the CPU tier's declared order.

agent_guidance.use_when: The routed experts do not all fit on the device beside the model's weights and the KV cache at the required context (recon's placement scenario sparse_device_host or sparse_device_host_disk), or the engine should not care whether they fit: it places them by itself
agent_guidance.avoid_when: A model without routed experts; an engine that must place experts by a rule of its own the decision tree does not take (pin it with the tier and misses options first)
provides: begin() decides the tier from the experts' bytes, the device's free memory less the model's own needs, and host memory
open() makes the device expert cache in the free memory past reserve_mib (or in a KV pool's spare bytes and idle pages) and builds the CPU tier, or copies every miss over the link
Recent residency beside the CPU tier: a missed expert is computed by the CPU now, copied in beside the round and served from the next round, in the slot of the expert routed longest ago

An elastic cache, a giver of the device's memory: every free byte the device does not keep (the run's VRAM headroom, Core's) after the warm requests; a prompt step gets the room a chunk of its size was measured to take, from the blocks torch's allocator kept of earlier prompts first, and the cache grows back after the prompt's last step
forward(layer, x, ids, weights, rows, prompt) per routed layer: decode plans, CPU posts and joins, prompt staging, captured rounds
Facts that say what it decided and why, telemetry with a one-line diagnosis, recorded routes for crit plugins offload --trace and for bench.py, which times the plugin alone on the engine's store
engine_supplies: begin(layers, experts, format, hidden, inter, device_bytes) before the loads, with the device bytes its pools still take
load() of every expert's stored tensors, as for experts that fit (skipped when a store file is complete)
open() after its pools; a KV pool allocated for the whole context lends its memory: made with spare=experts.spare_bytes(pool_bytes) and passed as open(lend=pool)
preserve: One arithmetic per path: the CPU tier's declared order on the device wherever the CPU computes misses, the kernel's tensor arithmetic where it does not
Every byte the model does not use for the cache, and never one it was not shown to be free: under WDDM an allocation past the device's memory moves to system memory instead of failing
Copies beside the round, never on a layer's path: the CPU tier computes the miss its layer needs
adapt: tier, misses and policy to pin a decision; reserve_mib is what a load's graphs and first prompts take (the run's VRAM headroom is the device's, Core's)
swaps and fill_blocks from a recorded trace: crit plugins offload --trace replays residency in seconds, bench.py times the plugin alone on the real experts in minutes
prompt_arithmetic tensor for a speed engine whose prefill the declared order bounds

code_files.purpose: ExpertOffload, the decision tree, the cache's memory through Core's step frames, FileStore and the diagnosis

The plugin alone on a bundle store file and a recorded routing trace: a captured graph a round as an engine runs it, the round's time, the CPU tier's share and time per missed expert, hits, misses and copies a round, for the options and each variant

Experts a GGUF checkpoint stores (format gguf): the slot layout of each layer's formats (wider layers in pieces, kept whole on the device), the bundles, gguf-rows over the slots (GgufRoutes, prompt chunks on its grouped GEMM) and the CPU tier in its declared order (GgufCpuTier)

requires.hardware: A CUDA GPU grouped-experts builds for; for the CPU path, the native CPU tier (host-expert-arithmetic's integer rows) and mapped pinned host memory
requires.model: Expert-routed models with SwiGLU experts in any format grouped-experts computes; the CPU path for NVFP4 (W4A4) and INT4 experts (native) and GGUF experts (in torch, gguf-rows' declared order)
requires.workload: Decode and verify rounds and prompt chunks through experts that do not all fit on the device

contract.input: The experts' geometry at begin(), each expert's stored tensors at load(), per routed layer the token rows, router ids and weights (ids -1 skipped)
contract.output: Each token's routed SwiGLU sum, FP32 [tokens][hidden], the bits of every expert on the device in the path's arithmetic
contract.ownership: The plugin owns the store, the cache, the CPU tier and the kernel workspaces; the model owns its pools (a KV pool it lends)
contract.failure: No grouped-experts kernel, experts that do not fit the chosen tier, a load after open() or of another format raise; a CPU tier that does not build falls back to link copies, recorded in the facts
contract.core_boundary: A plugin of the experts slot. Core tells it of the steps it ends (end_step) and frames every step with the device's memory and its captured rounds find it in its slot; the cache is an elastic range and a giver of the device's memory (crit_plugins.memory), which Core tells when the load is over

validation.host: Plugin tests: the host form is the reference bit for bit; the decision tree's tier, slots and miss path on given sizes; what a prompt step's memory follows; the diagnosis
validation.native: CUDA tests (tests/test_device.py, run on an RTX 5090): link misses give the all-device bits for decode and prompt chunks, CPU misses and the experts copied in beside the rounds the declared all-device bits, the disk tier reads its file, recorded routes
validation.performance: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next FP4-Local on one RTX 5090 and a Ryzen 5 9600 (WSL2). The plugin alone on 1,232 recorded rounds: 15.4 ms a round at 94% hits (ranked residency: 40.5 ms at 85%). In an engine, ten fresh prompts: 53.5 tok/s sampled and 60.0 greedy beside elastic KV pools, against 24.8 and 32.5 for the run engine whose experts it replaced
